title: Closed points in smooth charts representing finite-type stack points
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], fibred groupoids and $2$-fibre products mean [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A morphism is representable if every scheme base change is an algebraic space. Properties of representable maps are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. The point set $|\mathcal X|$ of an algebraic stack consists of field-valued objects modulo isomorphism after common field extension. A point is of finite type if it has a representative $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal X$ locally of finite type, where $K$ is a field [def-weil-field], and local finite type is tested on smooth scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every finite-type point $x$ of an algebraic stack $\mathcal X/S$, there are an affine scheme $U/S$, a smooth morphism $q:U\to\mathcal X$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and a closed point $u\in U$ mapping to $x$. With $k=\kappa(u)$ and $a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to U\to\mathcal X$, the map $a$ is locally of finite type. The algebraic space $R=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}k$, with source and target the projections and composition induced by composition of isomorphisms, is a groupoid over $S$ whose two projections to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are locally of finite type. Here $\kappa(u)$ is the residue field of $\mathcal O_{U,u}$.

proof.text: Choose a locally finite type representative $a_0:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal X$ of $x$ and a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:V\to\mathcal X$. Schemes are algebraic spaces, so the representable-diagonal theorem makes $a_0$ representable by algebraic spaces. Thus $Z=V\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}K$ is an algebraic space. Its map to $V$ is locally of finite type by base change of $a_0$; its map to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is surjective by base change of $p$. Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $e:E\to Z$. The chartwise calculus makes $e$ locally of finite type and the composite $h:E\to Z\to V$ locally of finite type. The space chart-test identifies this last property with the scheme property for $h$. The composite $E\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is surjective. Since a field spectrum has a point, $E$ is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 06FX (lemma-point-finite-type), (1) implies (2), first two sentences; expand finite type point selection using an etale scheme atlas of the pulled-back space.

proof.text: Take a nonempty affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq E$. A point of $W$ gives a proper prime ideal of $A$, so $A$ is nonzero. The maximal-ideal theorem gives a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$; its point $w$ is closed in $W$, since the only prime containing $\mathfrak m$ is $\mathfrak m$ itself. Put $L=\kappa(w)$. The canonical $r:\operatorname{Spec}L\to W$ is locally of finite type by condition (iii) of the scheme field-point criterion: use the affine neighbourhood $W$ and the degree-one extension $L/\kappa(w)$. The inclusion $W\hookrightarrow E$ is etale, hence locally of finite type. Since for scheme morphisms the chart-tested property is the scheme property (space chart-test), the composition clause of the chartwise calculus applies to these scheme maps: composition with $h$ makes $f:\operatorname{Spec}L\to V$ locally of finite type. Apply the field-point criterion again to $f$: its image $u$ is closed in some affine open $U\subseteq V$, and $L/\kappa(u)$ is finite. This uses no Jacobson or Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 06FX (lemma-point-finite-type), (1) implies (2), finite type point selection and affine shrinking; morphisms.tex Tag 01TA (lemma-point-finite-type), (2) iff (4); algebra.tex Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), (2).

proof.text: Let $j:U\hookrightarrow V$ be the inclusion and set $q=pj$. The open-immersion theorem makes $j$ etale; etale implies smooth and smooth morphisms compose, so $q$ is smooth. By the defining 2-isomorphism of $Z$, the field-valued maps $pf$ and $a_0b$ are isomorphic, where $b:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the composite through $W\to Z$. The field-morphism theorem writes $f$ as the canonical $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to V$ precomposed with $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(u)\to L)$; that canonical point factors through the open $U$. Also $b$ is induced by a field embedding $K\to L$. Consequently the representative of $q(u)$ and the chosen representative $a_0$ of $x$ become isomorphic over the common field $L$. By the point equivalence relation, $q(u)=x$. We have obtained the required affine $U$ and closed point $u$.

source.place: Tag 06FX (lemma-point-finite-type), conclusion of (1) implies (2); affine shrinking as in Tag 06FZ (lemma-identify-finite-type-points).

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(u)$ and let $c:\operatorname{Spec}k\to U$ be the canonical morphism. The scheme field-point criterion applies on the affine neighbourhood $U$, since $u$ is closed there and $k/\kappa(u)$ has degree one. Thus $c$ is locally of finite type. Smoothness makes $q$ locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type; by the space chart-test the scheme map $c$ is also locally of finite type in the chart-tested sense, so composition makes $a=qc$ locally of finite type. The representable-diagonal theorem also makes $a$ representable by algebraic spaces. Apply the self-relation theorem to $a$ (regarding $\operatorname{Spec}k$ as an algebraic space): $R=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}k$ is an algebraic space, and its two projections and composition of isomorphisms give a groupoid over $S$. Finally each projection $R\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a base change of the representable locally finite type map $a$ along $a$. Base-change stability in the chartwise calculus therefore proves local finite type for both projections.
